title: Volleyball: Wisconsin Badgers break even in Milwaukee, face difficult Pittsburgh slate - NewsBreak
text:
By Jarrett Guerrera Robin M Adams ,
14 hours ago The Wisconsin Badgers volleyball team is jumping back into the swing of things as the 2026 season is officially underway.
This past weekend the Badgers opened play at the AVCA First Serve event with matches against #3 Kentucky and #7 Louisville at the Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee. Wisconsin struggled against Kentucky, ultimately dropping the revenge game from a season ago in three sets. The Badgers bounced back with a statement 3-0 victory over the Cardinals to finish the weekend and start the season with a 1-1 record.
Wisconsin has a long way to go before facing a Big Ten opponent in #25 Oregon on September 24, and the next stop for the team will be in Pittsburgh for the Opening Spike Classic. The Badgers will face #5 Stanford on August 28 and #4 Pittsburgh on August 30 before heading into the Big Ten/SEC Challenge.
Pittsburgh was also in town for the AVCA First Serve event in Milwaukee, defeating Kentucky and Xavier while dropping just one set.
Wisconsin Badgers Travel to Pittsburgh to Face Another Strong Batch of Opponents Wisconsin head coach Kelly Sheffield watches his team while setter Morgan Van Wie (8), libero Jada Cerniglia (13) and outside hitter Trinity Shadd-Ceres (6) cheer during their match against Illinois Thursday, October 2, 2025 at the UW Field House in Madison, Wisconsin. Wisconsin beat Illinois 3-0. The Badgers are set to travel over to Pittsburgh to face both the Panthers and the Stanford Cardinal in two matches that should deliver fireworks. First up, Wisconsin will open the season for Stanford in a rematch from last December.
The Cardinal have yet to play a match this season and finished the 2025 campaign with a 3-1 loss to the Badgers in the NCAA Championship Regional Semifinal. Wisconsin had previously lost four-straight matches against Stanford before finally cracking the case on the biggest stage.
Stanford won the ACC last season in the second year the program was a member of the conference, and now in the third season the Cardinal have been predicted to repeat by the coaches of the conference. Team leaders Lizzy Andrew, Logan Parks, Spencer Etzler, Jordyn Harvey, and Julia Blyashov highlight the preseason All-ACC Team selections representing the Cardinal. Stanford has plenty to prove during the 2026 season after falling below postseason expectations a season ago.
Pittsburgh, on the other hand, is fresh off a pair of wins over Kentucky and Xavier in Milwaukee that displayed near complete dominance. The Panthers dropped one set to the Wildcats but handily defeated one of the top teams in the country before breezing through the Musketeers.
A season ago, the Panthers finished the year tied for the best record in the ACC and ended the season with a share of the conference title as Stanford received the other half. Once again the two programs are predicted to have a neck and neck battle for the top spot in the conference this upcoming season. Pittsburgh will look to continue their dominance against Big Ten opponents after going 4-1 last season.
For the Wisconsin Badgers, an early loss to Kentucky is not the end of the world but struggling to pull-out a win in Pittsburgh could be a cause for some concern. The Badgers are in the middle of one of the toughest stretches in the country with games against #3 Kentucky, #7 Louisville, #5 Stanford, #4 Pittsburgh, #17 Florida, # 8 Texas A&M, and #2 Texas in the span of three weeks. Coming out of the stretch without a scratch was never exactly expected and now the Badgers need to buckle up for the harder matches that are looming.
